PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Met.ConfigLabel: PainterlyNPR - Technical Pens: the Four Calibrated Line Widths
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Met.ConfigNote: The one place a pen width is decided. Four STAEDTLER Mars matic 700 tubular-nib pens, absolute widths on the finished printed sheet; which pen each part of the scene takes, the strongest that applies winning; what the Drawing Discipline and art direction may and may not do to a pen; and the technical and variable width modes.

PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pen.Note: The pens, lightest first. WidthMm is the line's final width on the printed sheet - never an addition to the base, never multiplied by a preset. Tier is the pen's place in the order (0 the base). The same keys, names and widths as ValeVision AURA's annotation pens.

M013.Name: Base lines
M013.Label: 0.13 mm
M013.Use: The foundation: every visible eligible line, vegetation, leaves, branches, grass, material patterns, hatching and fine linework

M018.Name: Minor features
M018.Label: 0.18 mm
M018.Use: Windows, doors, fences, joinery, glazing bars, smaller fittings and lettering

M025.Name: Structural lines
M025.Label: 0.25 mm
M025.Use: Walls, roofs, structural boundaries and significant architectural features

M035.Name: Profile lines
M035.Label: 0.35 mm
M035.Use: Dominant silhouettes, building outlines, the ground line and important object profiles

PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pen.BasePenNote: Every eligible stroke is drawn with it in the base buffer, whatever pen it is drawn with on the sheet
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pen.LetteringPenNote: Stroke-built lettering (38__Line__Lettering) is drawn with it

PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Sem.Note: Which pen a line of the scene takes, from what it belongs to: the object's Category, then a Material within it, then its Role, which only ever raises the profile pen. Pen is the line's own; Profile the pen its silhouette runs take (a much farther surface beside them); Ground the pen of the line where it meets the ground. Material indication, organic grammars, hatching, construction lines and the distant belt are base marks and never come here.

CategoriesNotes.Wall: A wall's edges are structural; its silhouette and its ground line are the building's outline
CategoriesNotes.Roof: Roof slopes, verges, ridges, dormers and chimney stacks; the pots on the stacks are fittings
CategoriesNotes.Porch: The oak frame is joinery, its outline a significant feature; its tiled roof is a roof
CategoriesNotes.Opening: Windows, doors and their joinery, the opening's own outline included
CategoriesNotes.Hardscape: Paths, kerbs, the road: landscape linework, the base pen

PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Sem.RolesNote: The drawing's subject: its profile is an important object profile. A role raises a pen, never lowers one
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Sem.DefaultNote: A category this table does not name draws with the base pen until someone names it: ordinary lines are 0.13 mm unless assigned a heavier pen
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Sem.PatternClassNote: An Authored line of this class or lower priority (3: Optional) drawn on a face - a plank joint, boarding - is a surface pattern: the base pen. A thin member's two arrises drawn as one line (a glazing bar's pair) is not: it keeps its element's pen

PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pro.Note: When a run of a line is its element's silhouette or ground line, and the Pen's sliders that once weighted them. In the technical mode a slider no longer multiplies a width: above its neutral value it lets the promotion happen, at or below it it does not. Every pen preset leaves them above.
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pro.ProfileShareNote: A run is a silhouette when more than this share of its samples has a much farther surface beside it
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pro.ShadeShareNote: A run has shade on one side when more than this share of its samples has
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pro.GroundHeightMNote: A straight hard edge lower than this is where the element meets the ground
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pro.ProfileAboveNote: Pen -> Silhouettes above x1: profile runs take their element's profile pen
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pro.GroundAboveNote: Pen -> Ground line above x1: ground lines take their element's ground pen
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Pro.ShadeInkNote: Pen -> Shadow side, in the technical mode: a line with shade on one side is weighted in ink, not width - its ink x (1 + this x the slider), at most full

PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Sim.Note: The Drawing Discipline's simplification (Keep, the shortest line, the Pen's Detail) and Lost in light never take a visible line away now: the line keeps its base pen and loses only a heavier one. Only occlusion, the paper (presence), a retired or unseen edge and a Detail suppression point take a line away. Off, a simplified or lit line keeps its heavier pen too.
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Sim.LitShareNote: A fragment more than this share lit on both sides (the old lost-in-light test, point by point) is drawn with the base pen

PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Poi.Note: Art direction moves a line between the four pens, never off them. A point's weight (a Focus point's touch heavier, a Line Control point's Weight and Emphasis) is counted in pen steps - each pen is about 1.39 times the last - and a step is taken once the weight is StepAt of the way to the next pen: a Focus point (x1.2) leaves the pen alone, a Line Control point at its x0.75 goes down one. Marks (indication, plants, hatching) keep the base pen; there a point's weight is ink.
PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Poi.StepAtNote: 0.5 would round to the nearest pen; 0.75 keeps a touch heavier on its pen

PainterlyNPR__TechnicalPens__Config__Mod.Note: Technical pens, the default: every stroke is drawn at exactly its pen's width; the presets, pressure and art direction change behaviour - ink, path, taper, breaks - never the width. Variable is the explicitly non-technical mode: pressure, the broad nib, line weight, the hierarchy, silhouette, ground and shadow-side weights and point weights modulate the pens' widths, never below the base pen. A preset never changes the mode.
